FROM MODEL COMPRESSION TO HARDWARE-AWARE AI
What comes after compression?
Previous techniques reduced:
Pruning
Reduce operations
Quantization
Reduce bits and energy/MAC
Knowledge Distillation
Reduce model size
Sparsity
Skip unnecessary computation
These techniques reduce a model's size and operation count — but a smaller model is not automatically a faster or more efficient one on real hardware.
THE NEXT CHALLENGE
A model can have fewer parameters and FLOPs — and still be inefficient on a particular device.
Different processors have different capabilities
Memory access can dominate energy use
Accelerators favor specific operators
Parallelism & data movement affect latency
Model design + hardware design must be considered together.

HW-NAS WORKFLOW
Five steps from target to architecture
01
Define hardware target
Smartphone · CPU · GPU · NPU · Microcontroller · Edge accelerator
02
Define constraints
Max latency · Max power · Max memory · Min accuracy
03
Generate architectures
Vary layers, kernel sizes, channels, operators, depth
04
Hardware evaluation
Measure or estimate latency, energy, memory
05
Select optimal architecture
Accuracy + Hardware Efficiency
Objective:  Best Architecture = Accuracy + Hardware Efficiency
HARDWARE-AWARE & ADAPTIVE AI
5

HW-NAS PRINCIPLE
Same model, different performance
A model may perform very differently depending on the target hardware.
ACCURACY vs. TARGET FIT
Model A
High accuracy
Slow on CPU
Model B
Slightly lower
Fast on CPU, very fast on NPU
Model C
Medium
Very fast on CPU
A model with slightly lower accuracy can be preferable if it gives much lower latency, lower power, better battery life, and higher throughput.

TINYML
AI on extremely small devices
TinyML runs machine-learning models on highly resource-constrained devices:
Microcontrollers
Sensors
Wearables
IoT devices
Battery-powered systems
TYPICAL CONSTRAINTS
Few KB/MB of memory  ·  Very low compute  ·  Limited battery  ·  Low clock frequency  ·  No continuous cloud link
EXAMPLE APPLICATIONS
Wake-word detection
Human activity recognition
Machine fault detection
Environmental monitoring
Gesture recognition
Main objective: useful intelligence with extremely low energy consumption.

EARLY-EXIT NEURAL NETWORKS
Not every input needs full computation
Add prediction points at intermediate layers — if the model is confident, it stops early.
Input
→
Layer 1
Exit 1?
→
Layer 2
Exit 2?
→
Layer 3
Exit 3?
→
Final
Classifier
If confident → stop early → save computation → save energy
WORKED EXAMPLE  ·  Full network = 100 energy units
Easy input:  exits after 30% of network → ≈30 energy units
Difficult input:  continues to 70% → ≈70 energy units
Eavg = Σ Pi · Ei
Pi = probability of exiting at stage i · Ei = energy consumed until that stage
HARDWARE-AWARE & ADAPTIVE AI
10

EARLY EXIT TRADE-OFF
Accuracy vs. energy
Higher confidence threshold
→
Fewer early exits
→
Higher accuracy
→
More computation
→
Higher energy
Lower confidence threshold
→
More early exits
→
Lower average energy
→
Potential accuracy loss
EARLY-EXIT SYSTEMS REQUIRE
Confidence estimation
Proper exit thresholds
Calibration
Validation on representative data
Key idea: spend more computation only when the input actually needs it.

LOW-RANK ADAPTATION
LoRA: reducing the cost of training
Fine-tuning large models is expensive: it requires large GPU memory, large optimizer states, high training energy, and long training time.
TRADITIONAL FINE-TUNING
Pre-trained model  →  update all parameters
→  High memory + high compute
LoRA
Pre-trained model  →  freeze original weights
→  train only small low-rank matrices
W' = W + ΔW      where      ΔW = BA
A, B = small matrices  ·  r = low rank  ·  r ≪ d  (d = original model dimension)
Only A and B are trained — the base model stays frozen.
HARDWARE-AWARE & ADAPTIVE AI
12

WHY LORA REDUCES TRAINING COST
Full fine-tuning vs. LoRA
FULL FINE-TUNING
Train 100% of model parameters
✕
Gradients
✕
Optimizer states
✕
Parameter updates
✕
Large GPU memory
LoRA
Train only low-rank adapter parameters
The base model remains frozen.
✓
Fewer trainable parameters
✓
Lower GPU & optimizer memory
✓
Faster fine-tuning, lower energy
✓
Multiple adapters share one base model
Important distinction:  LoRA primarily reduces training cost. After training, LoRA weights can be merged into the base model, avoiding extra inference layers in many deployments.

THE FINAL OBJECTIVE
Performance-per-Watt
Not simply maximum accuracy — instead:  useful performance per watt.
Accuracy
Does the model solve the task?
Latency
How quickly does it respond?
Energy
How much does each prediction cost?
Memory
Can it fit on the device?
Training cost
How expensive is adaptation?
Hardware utilization
Can hardware exploit model structure?
Design AI models not only for accuracy — but for where and how they will run.
